concepts.description_formal: A parametric curve in the plane is given by two functions x and y of a parameter t, whose values at each t are the coordinates of a point on the curve.
concepts.description_plain: Two functions of a parameter give the two coordinates of a moving point.
concepts.name: Curve defined by parametric equations

concepts.description_formal: For a parametric curve, dy/dx at a point equals dy/dt divided by dx/dt at the corresponding parameter value, provided dx/dt is not zero.
concepts.description_plain: The slope of the tangent is the rate of y divided by the rate of x.
concepts.name: Slope of a parametric curve as a quotient of derivatives

concepts.description_formal: The second derivative of y with respect to x for a parametric curve equals the derivative with respect to the parameter of dy/dx, divided by dx/dt.
concepts.description_plain: Differentiate the slope with respect to the parameter, then divide by dx/dt again.
concepts.name: Second derivative of a parametric curve
concepts.notation: second derivative of y with respect to x

concepts.description_formal: For a parametric curve on a parameter interval, the length of the curve is the definite integral of the square root of the sum of the squares of dx/dt and dy/dt over that interval.
concepts.description_plain: The length is the integral of the magnitude of the pair of rates.
concepts.name: Arc length of a parametric curve

concepts.description_formal: A vector-valued function of one variable is an ordered pair of real valued functions, and its value at each input is a vector in the plane.
concepts.description_plain: A vector function is just two ordinary functions written together.
concepts.name: Vector-valued function as a pair of component functions
concepts.notation: ordered pair or angle bracket notation

concepts.description_formal: The derivative of a vector-valued function is the vector of the derivatives of its components, and the derivative of position is velocity while the derivative of velocity is acceleration.
concepts.name: Derivative of a vector-valued function taken component by component

concepts.description_formal: The definite integral of a vector-valued function over an interval is the vector whose components are the definite integrals of the component functions.
concepts.description_plain: Integrate each component separately to get a vector.
concepts.name: Integral of a vector-valued function taken component by component

concepts.description_formal: Given a velocity vector and the position at one time, the position at another time is the initial position added componentwise to the definite integral of the velocity over the interval.
concepts.description_plain: Each coordinate is its starting value plus the accumulated change.
concepts.name: Particular position from a rate vector and an initial position
concepts.notation: position from velocity plus initial position

concepts.description_formal: For a particle in planar motion, speed at a time is the square root of the sum of the squares of the two velocity components.
concepts.description_plain: Speed is the length of the velocity vector, not either component.
concepts.name: Speed as the magnitude of the velocity vector
concepts.notation: speed as the magnitude of velocity

concepts.description_formal: For a particle in planar motion over a time interval, the definite integral of its speed over that interval is the total distance it travels.
concepts.description_plain: Integrating speed over the interval gives the length of the path travelled.
concepts.name: Total distance travelled as the integral of speed

concepts.description_formal: A particle moves toward a coordinate axis when the coordinate measured from that axis is positive and its derivative is negative, or negative with derivative positive.
concepts.description_plain: Each component sign says which way the particle is moving along that axis.
concepts.name: Direction of motion read from the signs of the velocity components

concepts.description_formal: For a curve given by r as a function of theta, the Cartesian coordinates of the point at angle theta are x equal r times the cosine of theta and y equal r times the sine of theta.
concepts.description_plain: The coordinates of a polar point are r times cosine and r times sine of the angle.
concepts.name: Polar to Cartesian relations
concepts.notation: x = r cos theta; y = r sin theta

concepts.description_formal: For r as a function of theta, dr/dtheta is the rate of change of the distance from the origin with respect to the polar angle, and its sign says whether the curve is moving away from or toward the origin.
concepts.description_plain: The derivative of r says how fast the distance from the origin changes with the angle.
concepts.name: Rate of change of r with respect to theta

concepts.description_formal: For a polar curve, dy/dx equals the derivative with respect to theta of r times the sine of theta divided by the derivative with respect to theta of r times the cosine of theta.
concepts.description_plain: Write x and y in theta, then take the quotient of their rates.
concepts.name: Slope of a polar curve in the plane

concepts.description_formal: For a polar curve r as a function of theta, the area of the region swept between two angles is one half the definite integral of the square of r with respect to theta over that interval.
concepts.description_plain: Sum the areas of thin circular sectors across the angle interval.
concepts.name: Area of a polar region as an integral of one half r squared
concepts.notation: one half the integral of r squared d theta

concepts.description_formal: For two polar curves with the outer one farther from the origin on an angle interval, the area between them is one half the definite integral of the square of the outer radius minus the square of the inner radius.
concepts.description_plain: Subtract the squares of the two radii inside one half the integral.
concepts.name: Area between two polar curves
concepts.notation: one half the integral of the difference of squares

concepts.description_formal: The angles bounding a region between two polar curves are the solutions of the equation setting the two radius functions equal on the interval of interest.
concepts.description_plain: The curves meet where their radii agree at the same angle.
concepts.name: Intersection angles of two polar curves

prerequisites.description_plain: Reading a position, velocity, or acceleration written as an ordered pair or with angle brackets, and labelling the two components when they are listed separately.
prerequisites.failure_signature: Student reports two correct components without saying which is which, or mixes the two orders within one response.
prerequisites.name: Reading vector and ordered pair notation for a position in the plane
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the BC-UNIT-09 essential knowledge statements.

prerequisites.description_plain: Reading cosine and sine of an angle as the horizontal and vertical coordinates on a circle of given radius, and solving a trigonometric equation for every solution in a stated interval.
prerequisites.failure_signature: Student cannot find the angles at which two polar curves meet, or finds only one of them.
prerequisites.name: Sine and cosine as coordinates and solving trigonometric equations on an interval
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the BC-UNIT-09 essential knowledge statements.

prerequisites.description_plain: Treating the argument of a trigonometric function as a radian measure, and keeping the calculator in radian mode when a model uses one.
prerequisites.failure_signature: Student produces values that are internally consistent but wrong throughout a question, with no algebraic error visible.
prerequisites.name: Radian measure as the calculator convention for trigonometric arguments
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the BC-UNIT-09 essential knowledge statements.

prerequisites.description_plain: Determining the interval of the parameter or the polar angle over which a curve or one loop of it is traced exactly once, and noticing when an interval repeats part of the curve.
prerequisites.failure_signature: Student integrates over an interval that covers a loop twice and reports double the area.
prerequisites.name: Deciding which parameter interval traces a curve exactly once
prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the BC-UNIT-09 essential knowledge statements.
